issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree in a suit concerning wakf property is not void for want of separate notice of the compromise when the Commissioner received notice of the suit, participated in it, and agreed to be removed as a defendant.
material_facts: The suit challenged the validity and enrolment of a wakf and sought relief concerning wakf property.
The Commissioner was joined as a defendant, received a summons with the plaint, appeared, filed a written statement, and contested the suit as collusive.
The Commissioner’s counsel was present when the Commissioner’s name was struck from the suit and did not object.
The suit was then decreed on compromise without a separate notice of the compromise petition to the Commissioner.
issues.conclusion: The decree was not void for want of a separate notice of the compromise petition, and the decision restoring the decree was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under ss. 69 and 70(1) of the Bengal Wakfs Act, 1934, the Commissioner is entitled to notice of a suit concerning wakf property, but the Act requires no separate notice of a compromise petition. A summons to a Commissioner joined as a party, with the plaint, sufficiently gives notice of the suit. The Commissioner’s participation and opportunity to resist the suit preclude treating the decree as void merely because no separate compromise notice was given. The Court distinguished State Wakf Board, Madras v. Abdul Azeez Sahib, 1968 AIR Mad 79; found Muzafar Ahmed v. Indra Kumar Das, 77 C.L.J. 159, did not support the Commissioner’s argument; and referred to Benoy Kumar Acharjee Choudhury v. Ahamma Ali, 46 C.W.N. 339, and The Commissioner of Wakfs, Bengal v. Shahbzada Mohammed Zahangir Shah, 48 C.W.N. 157, the latter supporting the effect of the Commissioner’s appearance and contest.

rule.if: wakf_property_suit and commissioner_summoned_as_party and commissioner_contested_suit and commissioner_agreed_to_removal and compromise_decree_entered

predicates.wakf_property_suit: The proceeding was a suit concerning wakf property.
predicates.commissioner_summoned_as_party: The Commissioner was joined as a party and received a summons giving notice of the suit.
predicates.commissioner_contested_suit: The Commissioner appeared and took steps to resist the suit.
predicates.commissioner_agreed_to_removal: The Commissioner did not object when the court removed him from the suit as a party.
predicates.compromise_decree_entered: The court entered a decree resolving the suit on the parties’ compromise.

issues.definition: When a suit concerning wakf property is brought to the Commissioner’s attention by summons, the Commissioner contests it, and then agrees to leave the suit before a compromise decree is entered, the decree is not void merely because no separate compromise notice was given.

issues.legal_issue: A Commissioner who already knew of a suit cannot rely on a later compromise as a fresh notice event to obtain a declaration that the decree is void for want of notice.
material_facts: The Commissioner received notice of the suit, appeared, and contested it before the compromise decree was entered.
After agreeing to be removed from the suit, the Commissioner applied to have the decree declared void on the ground that he had not received notice of the compromise.
issues.conclusion: The Commissioner could not obtain a declaration that the decree was void by claiming lack of a second notice after already having notice of the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 70(4) of the Bengal Wakfs Act, 1934, provides for a decree to be declared void in the absence of notice under s. 70(1). The Commissioner’s prior notice of the suit cannot be disregarded in favour of a later, separate notice event; no special notice of the compromise is required. The Court referred to the language of s. 70(4) and distinguished State Wakf Board, Madras v. Abdul Azeez Sahib, 1968 AIR Mad 79, where the circumstances concerning the Board’s notice were different.

predicates.proceeding_to_void_decree_for_lack_of_no: The proceeding seeks to have a decree declared void because the Commissioner was allegedly not given the required notice.
predicates.commissioner_knew_of_suit_before_decree: The Commissioner had notice of the suit before the decree was entered.

issues.definition: In a proceeding to void a decree for lack of notice, a Commissioner who already knew of the suit before the decree cannot obtain that result by claiming that a later event required a fresh notice.

issues.legal_issue: An objection based on the requirement of pre-suit notice under the Code of Civil Procedure does not arise in a later proceeding challenging the decree.
material_facts: In the proceeding concerning whether the decree was void, the Commissioner attempted to raise an objection based on s. 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.conclusion: The s. 80 objection could arise only in the original suit and not in the proceeding challenging the decree.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the objection under s. 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure as a matter arising in the original suit, not in the later proceeding before it.

predicates.collateral_decree_challenge: The proceeding is a later challenge to whether an existing decree is valid.
predicates.party_raises_pre_suit_notice_objection: A party relies in that later proceeding on an alleged failure to give notice before commencing the original suit.

issues.definition: When a party raises a pre-suit notice objection in a later challenge to a decree, that objection is not decided in the later challenge because it arises in the original suit.
